Distinguimos dos clases de acen­ tuación, una marcada, en la cual el ac ento incide en la vocal de la última silaba, y una no marcada o neutra, en la cual se acentúa la vocal de la penúltima sílaba o nin guna en particular. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding §4.3 'Acento' passage and the reduced-suffix note are verbatim in the text we hold layer (lines 659, 677 of); only the page numbers cannot be checked because the layer is unpaginated. (2) The classification rests on Adelaar 1982, a lexicon introduction by the language's sole authority, corroborated by held snippets of Adelaar & Muysken 2004 pp. 207 and 243, which independently state: default penultimate stress; final stress from word-final first-person -´y and from suffixes elided in word-final position (akšú-k < akšú-kta); a 'phonemic stress distinction' between final and penultimate. That matches our 'morphological' coding (penult default, final stress from identifiable morphological sources; final long vowel takes stress; opposition neutralized utterance-internally).
